clue.text: Still slip to lift over top of elasticated garment that's tight

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something means sitting above it, so this comes first
in a down clue, lifting the pieces turns them upwards so they read bottom to top

parts.note: still as a conjunction means but, nevertheless
a slip or blunder is a boob

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone notes a slip in their clothing: still, it lifts over the top of a tight elasticated top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' reverses BUT and BOOB together, giving BOOBTUB; 'top of' takes the E of 'elasticated' to finish. A boob tube is a strapless stretchy top.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapless, stretchy top that clings to the chest is a classic tight-fitting garment.

clue.text: Caged bird, perhaps, holding us up, 1940s' style

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within its letters

parts.note: a tit kept in a zoo would be a caged bird, so ZOO plus TIT

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A caged bird somehow delays us, in a scene with a 1940s flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns 'us' around before it is held inside. The zoot suit, with baggy high-waisted trousers and a long jacket, was a 1940s fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoot suit was a flamboyant outfit strongly associated with 1940s jazz culture, so it names a style of that decade.

clue.text: Vessel in difficult situation, conflict

parts.note: being in a jam is being in a difficult situation
a jar is a clash or disagreement

explanation.surface: A ship caught up in a tricky situation during a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass container for preserves is a vessel in the sense of something that holds contents.

clue.text: Potential wife, double trouble!

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so its letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: A man contemplates a prospective wife and foresees twice the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double trouble' reads as a stock phrase, but 'trouble' is the anagram signal working on 'double'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a noun, the hyphenated adjective describes someone aspiring or potential, as in an aspiring author.

clue.text: Sweet, short and round

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a pudding; a rolled steamed pudding

explanation.surface: A description of a little confection: sugary, small and spherical.
explanation.walkthrough: A roly-poly is a traditional British pudding of suet pastry spread with jam and rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names both a rolled jam pudding (a dessert, or sweet) and a podgy, rotund figure.

clue.text: Go with man like mad, embracing very intimate experience

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap around the extra piece
going mad means going wild, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to go with a man passionately, holding tight, for something very intimate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like mad' looks like one phrase, but 'like' is part of the fodder and only 'mad' signals the anagram; 'embracing' then wraps it around V.
explanation.definitionFit: Sex is about the most intimate experience two people can share, so the phrase is a fair euphemistic description.

clue.text: Last characters in ski lift, almost every one I see on the slope

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the next two words is taken
almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: every one together means all
C sounds like see, and stands for it in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A skier describes the last people on the ski lift, nearly everyone, as seen on the slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last characters in' takes I and T from 'ski lift'; 'almost' cuts ALL to AL; then I and C (the letter named by 'see').
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type leans to the right, so characters set that way are printed on a slant.

clue.text: A shade over the pond, a complete state

parts.note: over the pond, in America, a shade or colour is spelt without the U
to do a task is to complete it

explanation.surface: A transatlantic colour that marks out an entire state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the pond' means in the US, where colour is spelt COLOR.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty constituent states of the USA, in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: European city left in the midst of floods

indicators.note: the one piece sits inside the other
the middle letters of the word are taken, here the central pair

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A European city has been abandoned amid flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is not a direction to drop letters but the nautical port side.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, the Portuguese city famous for port wine, is traditionally called Oporto in English.

clue.text: Oddly, blonde is turning heads in story of life after death

indicators.note: the heads of the words are their first letters, read in order

explanation.surface: A strange tale: a blonde turns heads in a story about the afterlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but it is just one of the four words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper obituary tells the story of someone's life and is published after they die.

clue.text: Setter describing a clanger, perhaps, as owner of large corporation

parts.note: a jelly is something that sets, so it is a setter
a bell is a clanger, and bell-y, meaning like a bell, could describe it

explanation.surface: The crossword setter describes a blunder, perhaps one made by the boss of a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jocular word for a paunch, so its large owner is a fat person; a clanger here is a bell, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fat-bellied person is jokingly called this, and corporation is a humorous old word for a pot belly.

clue.text: Friendly and unfriendly types confused

parts.note: a friendly type is one who embraces people, a hugger
a mugger, who attacks and robs, is a decidedly unfriendly type

explanation.surface: Warm and hostile kinds of people are all mixed up together.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated phrase means muddled or disorderly, as well as secretive.

clue.text: Hero of the South, broadly speaking?

indicators.note: speaking says the word for broadly is heard, not written

parts.note: broadly means generally, on the whole

explanation.surface: A loose description of some Southern hero, broadly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadly speaking' looks like a stock phrase, but splits into the synonym and the sound signal. Robert E Lee commanded the Confederate army in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert E Lee, the Confederate commander, was the great military hero of the American South.

clue.text: Close relationship with British and Italian church

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A close relationship involving a Briton and an Italian church.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a blend for an intense non-sexual friendship between two men, a close relationship.

clue.text: Convert yearned for clerical office

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A religious convert longed for a post in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or position held by a dean, a senior cleric of a cathedral, has this name.

clue.text: Cultivate shrubs with one hollow plant

indicators.note: cultivating land works it over, so these letters are turned into a new order
a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: grow shrubs together with a single hollow-stemmed plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' reduces ONE to OE; 'Cultivate' rearranges SHRUBS with OE.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub that bears roses is a garden plant.

clue.text: Sharp instrument, point getting round to puncture you

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: puncturing goes into something, so one piece breaks into the other

parts.note: ye is the old word for you
a ring is round, a circle

explanation.surface: A sharp tool approaches, with its point coming round to pierce you.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypodermic needle used for injections is a sharp medical instrument.

clue.text: Europeans creasing pants

indicators.note: pants as a verb, or as British slang for rubbish, signals the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Some Europeans are crumpling their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers but rearranges CREASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Greeks, people of Greece, are Europeans.

clue.text: More than one grave line in some music

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: bars are measures, units of a piece of music
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A solemn line appears in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads like a solemn tempo marking, but it is a burial mound; barrows are prehistoric burial mounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient burial mounds are called barrows, so the plural means several graves.

clue.text: Mother does the housework? That's attractive!

parts.note: a char is a cleaner, so one who does the housework is a char: 'char is'
Ma is mother

explanation.surface: Someone admires a mother who keeps house.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Mother does the housework' as 'char is Ma': Ma is the cleaning lady. A char is a British term for a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism is the quality that makes someone attractive to others; the exclamation points to it.

clue.text: Feeling around a buttock and thigh

indicators.note: the one word goes around the letter

parts.note: a hunch is a feeling or intuition

explanation.surface: Someone feels around a person's bottom and thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: The haunch is the hip region of a body, taking in the buttock and the upper thigh.

clue.text: See 12
Old people won't necessarily answer

parts.note: something that won't necessarily happen may happen

explanation.surface: Elderly folk don't always reply.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient civilisation of Central America were a people of old.

clue.text: Reportedly, actress Elizabeth with strapping figure producing commotion

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Elizabeth Hurley is an English actress and model
strapping means burly, of a big strong build

explanation.surface: An actress with a powerful build causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming phrase means a noisy disorderly bustle, an uproar.

clue.text: See 2
Face among images I deleted

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit among those of the following words

explanation.surface: A face has been removed from some pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a surface or face of an object, as in the faces of a cube.

clue.text: Entrance, one admitting first of crew on ship

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
admitting lets something in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of the word

parts.note: SS means steamship

explanation.surface: An entrance where someone lets in the leader of the crew boarding a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is a means of entry, as in a side access to a building.

clue.text: Democrat in flying US party

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: winging means flying

explanation.surface: A Democrat is jetting off to a party in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingding is American slang for a lively, lavish celebration.
